Ransomware Attack Disrupts Turkish Technology Hardware Industry Operations

A large-scale ransomware attack is currently impacting several major firms in Turkey’s Technology Hardware industry, with ongoing disruptions to manufacturing operations and business systems reported on Thursday. The attack, which began late Tuesday night, has targeted the internal IT networks of multiple hardware manufacturers, causing widespread outages across production sites in the industrial districts of Istanbul, Izmir, and Bursa.

Industry sources describe the attack as “highly coordinated” and say it has encrypted access to design files, production schedules, and inventory management systems. Among the affected companies are EksiTech, Miratek, and Datatek Elektronik, all of which have confirmed partial shutdowns of their assembly lines as a result of the incident.

“Our teams are working in coordination with cybersecurity experts and law enforcement to contain the attack and restore systems,” said Selim Kurt, Chief Operations Officer of Miratek, in a statement. “At this time, we have halted production at two facilities as a precautionary measure, and administrative staff are unable to access key business applications.”

Several other firms in the sector have also reported difficulties. Workers at EksiTech’s Gebze facility were instructed to remain home until further notice, while Datatek Elektronik temporarily suspended output at its main Istanbul site. “We are prioritizing the safety of our data and the wellbeing of our employees,” a Datatek spokesperson said.

The Turkish Technology Hardware Manufacturers’ Association issued a statement urging all member firms to review their digital security protocols. “This incident underscores the critical importance of robust cybersecurity infrastructure for our industry,” said Association President Aylin Demir. “We are monitoring the situation closely and supporting affected firms.”

Analysts estimate that, depending on the duration of the outage, the attack could result in significant delays for ongoing projects and product deliveries. “The immediate impact is on day-to-day operations, but prolonged shutdowns could affect the sector’s competitiveness,” noted Haluk Yılmaz, a technology industry consultant based in Ankara.

At the time of writing, investigations into the origin and scale of the attack are ongoing, and affected firms have not yet received any formal ransom demands. The full impact on Turkey’s Technology Hardware industry remains to be seen as companies work to restore normal operations.
